newsitem.title: UK: N.Irish police warn of guerrilla threat.
newsitem.headline: N.Irish police warn of guerrilla threat.

text.p: Northern Irish police on Friday urged the public to be on the alert for possible guerrilla attacks after a spate of recent arms and explosives finds.
"Police are warning the public to be particularly vigilant in light of the recent increase in terrorist activity," the Royal Ulster Constabulary (RUC) said in a statement.

"The RUC is especially concerned that there is a threat facing the community at this time as demonstrated by recent incidents in Counties Fermanagh, Armagh and Londonderry, coupled with finds of terrorist munitions including incendiary devices."

The Irish Republican Army (IRA) killed a soldier in a car bomb attack on Britain's military headquarters in October, and a splinter group, the Irish Continuity Army Council, made an unsuccessful bid in November to set off a another outside a police base in Londonderry, the province's second city.

Both groups say that they are fighting to end rule by Britain. The province's 60 percent Protestant majority strongly support links with London and reject the republicans' aim to achieve an all-Ireland state ruled from Dublin.
The IRA abandoned a 17-month ceasefire in February, setting off the first of a string of bombs on mainland Britain.
Police in London on Thursday appealed for information about a truck which they said the IRA may have used to transport bomb-making equipment on mainland Britain.
In recent weeks in Northern Ireland, police have uncovered quantities of explosives and bomb making items and said that guerrillas tried to lure them into a mortar-bomb attack in Belfast.
The IRA has refused appeals by Britain, Ireland and the United States to call a new ceasefire to win a seat at peace talks for its Sinn Fein political arm.
